description: FS-GG typed coordination engine — the schedulability model behind `fsgg-coord` as one total function over a board-state snapshot, plus the typed IO layer that drives it. It IS the coordination tool (ADR-0034/ADR-0040): the `fsgg-coord` shim resolves and execs it; there is no bash left to shadow.
releaseNotes:
0.63.0 — filing guidance now requires typed validated intake, while the coordination CLI isolates BoardOps registration behind its owned boundary.

WHAT MOVED, AND WHY IT IS A MINOR. The packed Kit and Drivers change the executable filing recipes
consumers receive: `p-add`, `padd-item`, `cross-repo-coordination`, and `pnext-item` now construct the
complete `fsgg.coord.intake/v1` envelope, run `intake validate` before `intake apply`, and reserve direct
issue creation for an explicit recorded break-glass path (.github#2736). The semantic skill gate rejects
both `command gh api -X POST .../issues` bypasses and recipes that apply before validation, so the
prescription and its executable enforcement move together.

The CLI package also carries the BoardOps registration extraction from .github#2726. The program edge
now composes the BoardOps-owned handlers instead of retaining a second command-family registry, and the
`intake validate` registration reaches the pure application route without requiring GitHub credentials;
`intake apply` and every other live operation still use the authenticated dispatcher. This fixes the
tokenless validation path without changing its typed receipt or exit contract. The coherent-set policy
cuts every release as a MINOR, and all three packages therefore move together from the newest complete,
published 0.62.0 set to 0.63.0.

0.62.0 — the per-receiver operation lock gains a production caller, and `delivery` posts the merge election it grounds the authorization in.

WHAT MOVED, AND WHY IT IS A MINOR. Measured against 0.61.0, the newest version any consumer can
actually restore. `src/FS.GG.Coord.Core/Protocol.fs` is BYTE-IDENTICAL across the span, so no reported
field, result name or exit code changes meaning. Two receiver-observable things move, both purely
additive, and either alone would carry the line.

First, the CLI verb surface gains `op-lock acquire <item> <generation> <receiver> <op>` and
`op-lock release <receiver>` (.github#2312). This is the half of the per-receiver dispatch lock that
did not exist: at 0.61.0 `OpLock.acquire` had ZERO production callers and `OpLock.release` was absent
from the signature file and therefore private, so the dispatch broker's step-5 refusal was unreachable
BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by policy. The four positionals are `Operation.compose`'s own arguments;
the `dispatch:` prefix is derived from `Operation.wire` and round-tripped rather than spelled twice;
grant and opkey come from one `compose` call; the key is composed BEFORE the lock is taken; contended
exits 6 and every other failure exits 1; `release` verifies the holder rather than re-deriving a
winner. `FSGG_COORD_OP_LOCKS` selects the lock subjects, mirroring `FSGG_COORD_CHORE_LOCKS`.

Second, `delivery` now POSTS a `fsgg:merge-election` marker and writes an authorization GROUNDED in it,
carrying six fields rather than four — `opkey` and `grant` join `v`, `item`, `gen` and `head`
(.github#2395). The election is append-only and never deleted, so a transport failure between the two
writes leaves a durable fact the next call reuses rather than a half-taken lease. The receiver-visible
consequence is that `check-claim-fence`'s check 4 — the lowest-id election bearing this operation key —
IS NOW REACHED. It was not merely failing before: a four-field authorization was refused at check 1
for missing fields, so control never arrived at check 4, and the workflow's own operator note predicted
a red that could not occur. Both halves are observed in production on a real pull request.

ALSO SHIPPED, NOT YET REACHABLE. `FS.GG.Coord.Core` gains `fsgg.coord.churn-reading/v1` — a schema and
validator for the board-churn reading's six required elements, with the four pathology fields as tagged
unions so `searchedNotFound` (carrying the search performed) cannot be confused with `notSearched`
(carrying why not). Its `scripts/fsgg-coord` verb is NOT wired in this release and the shipped docs say
so plainly; .github#2774 tracks it. Nothing consumes the validator through the CLI at 0.62.0.

REPO-INTERNAL, RECORDED FOR COMPLETENESS: a signature-coverage gate that scores existence as an error
and substance as a warning (.github#2731), the merge-gate producer's observe-only reporting corrected to
derive which check fired rather than predict it (.github#2719), and a dispatch-broker transcription
differential executing the engine and the workflow over 48 vectors (.github#2720). None changes a
published surface.

PRIOR 0.61.0 — a `Kind` dimension separating closeable work from standing items, and a lifecycle-reducer exemption for every non-`work` kind.

WHAT MOVED, AND WHY IT IS A MINOR. Measured against 0.60.0, the newest version any consumer can actually
restore. Two receiver-observable things move, and either alone would carry the line.

First, the board gains a `Kind:` body-line sentinel with a closed four-value vocabulary — `work`,
`anchor`, `register`, `directive` — in the same grammar as `Paths:`, `Class:` and `Blocked on:`
(.github#2712). A row declaring a non-`work` kind is EXEMPT FROM THE LIFECYCLE REDUCER ENTIRELY: the
reducer projects no `Status` for it and persists no lifecycle watermark — no park, no promotion, no
`Done`. The scheduler refuses it with a new verdict, `not-a-unit-of-work`, that names the kind rather
than reporting the row's column. Class anchors, registers and directives have no completion condition,
and one `Status` lifecycle was being applied to all three.

AN ABSENT `Kind:` LINE MEANS `work`, so every existing row behaves exactly as it did at 0.60.0. This is
the opposite default from an absent `Class:` line, deliberately: an unset class is a triage omission
that must stay loud, while an unset kind is the common and correct answer.

Second, `ready --json` and the board reads gain two fields per row: `kind` (the board column, a
projection of the body line, `null` until an operator creates the field) and `commentCount` — observable
REGISTER DEPTH, so a host can tell a healthy inbox from a long backlog without opening the issue. It
rides the existing board page query as a connection `totalCount` and selects no nodes, so the board read
costs what it did before. A `KIND-PROJECTION-LAG` chore writes the column from the body, and is withheld
behind one diagnostic while the project declares no `Kind` field.

COSTS AND LIMITS. `claim` costs one further REST read per invocation — the item's body, for its `Kind:`
line, which cannot be taken from the board column without letting a lagging projection decide, nor from
the persisted watermark without freezing the exemption. It is bounded by items claimed rather than by
board size and is pinned by a test. A row whose body could not be read is treated exactly as at 0.60.0.

WHAT SHIPS IN THE KIT AT THIS VERSION. The `KIND-PROJECTION-LAG` remedy row in `check-board`, and the
`not-a-unit-of-work` verdict in the `intra-repo-parallel-work` protocol projection.

WHY THIS PACKAGE MOVES WITH THE KIT. The three packages resolve one scalar (`FsggCoherentSetVersion`,
`Directory.Build.props`) by construction (.github#2402), so all three ship at this same version.

STANDING ADVISORIES — these are NOT this release's notes, and they do not age out.

Two published FS.GG.Coord.Cli versions must never be adopted. Their own listings are immutable and
cannot be corrected, so the NEWEST listing is the only channel that can say so — and an unpinned
`dotnet tool install` resolves the newest version, which makes this the entry a consumer reads.
They live in their own MSBuild property (`FsggStandingAdvisories`) rather than inside the release
narrative below, so that trimming the narrative and deleting a warning are different edits
(.github#2579). `scripts/check-engine-release-notes.py` refuses a listing that stops referencing
this property or empties it; 4fccc76d deleted these warnings once while that gate was green.

DO NOT ADOPT 0.50.1. It is a permanent two-of-three set. The 0.50.1 cut published `FS.GG.Kit` and
`FS.GG.Drivers` to both feeds and was then REFUSED for this package by `check-engine-release-notes`
(`.github#1762`), which correctly flagged that the release notes still began with `0.50.0`. Both
sibling packages were already immutable at 0.50.1 and `.github#1772`'s sibling-tag precondition
requires all three tags to name the SAME commit, so 0.50.1 could not be completed from a corrected
tree. `FS.GG.Kit 0.50.1` and `FS.GG.Drivers 0.50.1` should not be adopted on their own; adopt
0.50.2, which is the whole set cut from one commit.

DO NOT ADOPT 0.50.5. It is a permanent two-of-three set, the same shape and the same cause as
0.50.1. `FS.GG.Kit 0.50.5` and `FS.GG.Drivers 0.50.5` published to both feeds; this package's
publish was then REFUSED by `check-engine-release-notes` because the notes still began with
`0.50.4` while `Version` had moved to `0.50.5`. Correcting that needs a new commit, and the
sibling-tag precondition requires all three tags at the SAME commit, so 0.50.5 could not be
finished from a corrected tree — re-cutting it is the re-pack divergence `.github#2240` documents.
Adopt 0.50.6.

DO NOT ADOPT 0.52.0. It is a different permanent partial set: `FS.GG.Kit` and `FS.GG.Drivers`
published to both feeds, and `FS.GG.Coord.Cli` published to the org feed before nuget.org rejected
its 37,279-character `PackageReleaseNotes`. NuGet versions are immutable and re-packing corrected
bytes under 0.52.0 would make the same version identify different artifacts. Adopt 0.53.0, the next
coherent set cut from corrected source. All three partial sets are recorded in
`registry/dependencies.yml`.

FULL PER-VERSION HISTORY IS SERVED BY THE REGISTRY, NOT REPEATED HERE (`.github#2579`). Every
published version's own notes remain readable, permanently, on that version's own listing at
https://www.nuget.org/packages/FS.GG.Coord.Cli — and each cut's evidence is recorded in
`registry/dependencies.yml` and `registry/CHANGELOG.md` at https://github.com/FS-GG/.github.

The release notes remain bounded: previous-version history stays on the registry listings and only
the standing safety advisories carry forward.
